subsystems.name: Preservation and fixation
subsystems.role: freeze the brain's structure in place, down to synapses, before it decays.

subsystems.name: Sectioning
subsystems.role: slice the roughly 1.3 litre organ into millions of ultrathin sections thin enough to image.

subsystems.name: Volume imaging
subsystems.role: capture every synapse at nanometre resolution.

subsystems.name: Image reconstruction
subsystems.role: turn millions of separate images into one 3D volume.
parts: machine-learning segmentation of neurons and synapses

subsystems.name: Connectome graph
subsystems.role: the wiring diagram plus the weight of every connection.
parts: synapse list with size and type

subsystems.name: Dynamical model
subsystems.role: give the graph physiology so it behaves like the original brain.

subsystems.name: Compute substrate
subsystems.role: run roughly 86 billion neurons and 100 trillion synapses fast enough to be useful.

buildSteps.title: Obtain and fix the brain
buildSteps.detail: Within minutes of death the tissue must be perfused with fixative so synaptic structure does not degrade. This applies to any animal brain; for a specific human it also needs a lawful, consented route.

buildSteps.title: Stain and embed
buildSteps.detail: Heavy-metal stains are infused to give membranes electron contrast, then water is replaced and the tissue cast in hard resin so it can be cut.

buildSteps.title: Cut into ultrathin sections
buildSteps.detail: A diamond knife shaves the block into sections tens of nanometres thick — millions of them for a whole human brain — collected on tape or wafers.

buildSteps.title: Image the sections
buildSteps.detail: Each section is scanned in a multi-beam electron microscope at a few nanometres per pixel, producing a 2D image stack. Data volume for a whole human brain would exceed any existing data infrastructure by many orders of magnitude.

buildSteps.title: Align and segment
buildSteps.detail: The images are registered into one volume, then machine-learning models trace every neurite and mark every synapse, with people checking the errors.

buildSteps.title: Build the connectome graph
buildSteps.detail: Neurons become nodes, synapses become weighted edges, and cells are sorted into types by shape, targets and molecular markers where those are known.

buildSteps.title: Assign physiology
buildSteps.detail: Each cell type is given a realistic model with the right membrane properties, and synapses are assigned strengths — most of which cannot be read from anatomy alone.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate against real activity
buildSteps.detail: The model is run and its output compared with recorded brain activity. At whole-human scale no ground truth exists, so this step is currently impossible.

buildSteps.title: Run and use the twin
buildSteps.detail: If it works, the twin executes on a large computer and can be probed for experiments. A full human brain in real time is far beyond today's fastest machines.

prerequisites.why: complete connectomes exist only for small animals; a whole human brain is roughly six orders of magnitude larger in volume than the largest published datasets.

prerequisites.tech: Preservation that survives the scanning pipeline
prerequisites.why: fixed and plastic-embedded tissue can be imaged, but keeping a whole human brain intact through millions of sections is unsolved.
machine learning can trace neurons in fly and mouse data, but human-scale proofreading cost remains prohibitive.
anatomy gives wiring, not the strengths, time constants and neuromodulation that decide what a circuit actually computes.
simulating 86 billion neurons and 100 trillion synapses at millisecond resolution in real time is far beyond demonstrated capability.

pathway.milestone: complete wiring diagrams for small nervous systems, such as the 302-neuron nematode (1986) and the adult fruit fly brain (2024)
pathway.unlocks: methods for stitching and segmenting large connectomes.

pathway.milestone: whole mouse brain at synaptic resolution, plus macroscale human maps from diffusion MRI such as the Human Connectome Project
pathway.unlocks: a bridge between wiring and measured brain activity.

pathway.milestone: human cortical tissue blocks imaged and modelled functionally
pathway.unlocks: validation of whether structure alone predicts dynamics in human tissue.

pathway.milestone: whole human connectome, requiring a step change in sectioning, imaging, storage and analysis
pathway.unlocks: a static digital replica — still not a working mind.

pathway.milestone: validated whole-brain emulation running in real time
pathway.unlocks: in-silico drug and disease testing. Treat 'consciousness backup' as philosophy, not engineering: a faithful copy would be a separate entity, not a continuation of the original person.
